newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: NETANYAHU SAYS HEBRON DEAL IS NEAR.
newsitem.headline: NETANYAHU SAYS HEBRON DEAL IS NEAR.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Monday that a deal was very close on the vexed question of Hebron, a key issue blocking the peace process between Israel and the Palestinians.
"It is very close to conclusion," Netanyahu told journalists at a summit of the 54-nation Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), which Israel is attending as an observer.

But the Israeli premier used a series of bilateral meetings with European leaders on the fringes of the summit to urge them to bring greater pressure on Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to clinch a final agreement on the West Bank city.
"Netanyahu pointed out that Europe could not give Arafat the feeling that, no matter what he does, he will always have their automatic support," government spokesman Moshe Fogel told journalists.

The right-wing Israeli leader, who has been accused by Arab countries of jeopardising lasting peace by seeking to renegotiate existing accords, gave no further details of how the diplomatic breakthrough on Hebron might come.

Under a peace deal with the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO), Israel should have already turned over most of Hebron, where about 400 Jewish settlers live in heavily armed compounds surrounded by 100,000 Arabs, to Palestinian self-rule.

But the pullback has been delayed by Israeli demands, following a wave of suicide bombings earlier this year, that its armed forces should have the right to pursue suspects in Palestinian-controlled areas.
But the Israelis also accuse the Palestinians of raising new elements in the talks and delaying their conclusion.

The Israeli tough line on Hebron, together with Netanyahu's refusal to trade occupied Arab land for peace -- the basic principle of the 1991 Madrid Middle East peace deal -- has infuriated the Palestinians and their Arab backers.

The Arab League, meeting in Cairo on Sunday, condemned Israel's expansion of settlements on occupied territory and warned the Jewish state that such practices could destroy the entire Middle East peace process.
In Lisbon Netanyahu met a number of government leaders from Europe and North America, including U.S. Vice President Al Gore and French President Jacques Chirac.
"It is clear to the U.S. who is holding back the agreement and that basically it is being held back by the Palestinians. This was clear to the Americans," Netanyahu's spokesman said.
But his meeting with Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa scheduled for Monday morning was postponed until Tuesday. No reason was given for the delay.

Chirac had urged the Israeli leader during a 40-minute meeting to make a gesture towards the Palestinians to improve the "climate of mutual incomprehension" that was complicating the search for a lasting peace, French presidential spokeswoman Catherine Colonna told reporters.
